Re-checking formula: Monthly profit = (Price - variable cost) * units sold - fixed cost, where units sold = min(demand at that price, 1300 capacity). Variable cost = $9, fixed = $12,000.

- $19: margin = 19-9 = $10. sold = min(2727,1300) = 1300. Profit = 10*1300 - 12000 = 13000-12000 = $1,000
- $24: margin = 24-9 = $15. sold = min(1385,1300) = 1300. Profit = 15*1300 - 12000 = 19500-12000 = $7,500
- $29: margin = 29-9 = $20. sold = min(954,1300) = 954. Profit = 20*954 - 12000 = 19080-12000 = $7,080
- $34: margin = 34-9 = $25. sold = 146. Profit = 25*146 - 12000 = 3650-12000 = -$8,350
- $39: margin = 39-9 = $30. sold = 100. Profit = 30*100 - 12000 = 3000-12000 = -$9,000

All margins are positive, so producing up to min(demand,capacity) is optimal. Highest profit is $24 at $7,500.
